passage.title: Why do we need arts?
passage.subtitle: Sometimes people question why we need ’the arts’; what functions do art, music, dance and literature serve?
paragraphs: A. Imagine a world in which people spend hours working in offices or factories, and then go home in the evening to sit down to dinner, after which they sleep until it’s time to get up and work again. In this world, people do not read or watch TV, listen to music, play computer games or have pictures to decorate their homes. In fact, there are no pictures in this world – not even advertisements are illustrated, but all are words, and very plain ones at that, with no playfulness left in them. The buildings are completely functional without a single decorative feature anywhere, and there is no music to dance to and enjoy. Such a world is a world without the arts in any form.

B. To ask what the arts are good for is not exactly the same as asking what their purpose is. The arts do not have to have a purpose – they do not exist in order to teach, to make a moral point, to entertain, to distract, to amuse, to support a revolution, to disgust, to challenge, to stimulate or to cheer; they exist chiefly for their own sake. It is artists, not the arts as such, that may have an aim in mind, and their aim may be to do any of the things just listed. But equally, artists may just make a work of art because they feel compelled to. Because the work is its own justification, no aim or goal is necessarily required to explain or, still less, to justify its existence.

C. But to say that the arts do not have to serve an aim beyond themselves, even though they may sometimes do so, is not to say that they are good for nothing. On the contrary, as such an important part of human experience, they are good for many things. The distinction here lies between things that are instrumental and things that are ends in themselves. An instrument exists for something beyond itself – namely, for what it can be used to do. We know that pictures are used as instruments in advertising, and the objective is always to persuade us to buy something. Similarly, music can be written chiefly to accompany dancing, or as a soundtrack to a movie. A play can be written to point out to the theatre audience a social injustice or other problems that should be dealt with. But even though the arts can sometimes be instrumental, that fact is not essential to their nature. What the arts are ’good for’ arises from their being an end in themselves, or more accurately, representing many different things that are valuable for their own sakes – such as, for instance, the creation of beauty.

D. The phrase ’the arts’ includes painting, sculpture, music, literature, dance and theatre performance, and whatever else (to quote the famous US artist Andy Warhol) anyone can get away with in calling their creation a contribution to ’the arts’. But the generalisation that the arts, whatever else they are, are always an end in themselves, applies to them all. The arts are one major form of response to the world. They are often an attempt to capture an aspect of the world, to draw attention to something about it to comment on it, to present a surprising or fresh angle on it, to represent it for the sake of exploring something about it, or enjoying or celebrating it. They can help people to focus on, for example, the colour or shape of an object, its eccentricity or typicality, and the interest or perhaps disgust it provokes in them.

E. For a loose comparison, think of laughing at a joke. We do not laugh so that we can achieve a further goal – in order to be healthy or relaxed, say, even if we thereby succeed in being healthier or more relaxed – but simply because the joke has elicited that reaction. But although it is merely a reaction, laughing is, in fact, good for something nevertheless; it does make people feel better. The arts are a reaction in the same way. French artist Cézanne painted Mont Sainte-Victoire repeatedly because he was fascinated by it, not because he thought that painting it would say something about politics or society or human hopes. Being fascinated by something, attracted to it, repelled by it, keen to reveal an unusual aspect of it, are all responses to that thing; the making of the arts is one outstanding way of expressing such responses.

F. But the arts are a response not only to things in the world but also to experience of the world, which lies inside the artist himself. And they are also often an expression of what presses from within the artist without being elicited by externals. Music is a prime example. A symphony, unless it is devised to represent bird song, rain, the sea and the like, is an abstract expression of a composer’s conception. We may be able to describe what the Russian composer Tchaikovsky is doing in his ballet music, but how can we describe what he is expressing in his piano concertos? Composers may experiment with melody and rhythm in very abstract, sometimes mathematical, ways.

G. When artists get to work responding to and expressing ideas, whether or not they also want to make a point, entertain, distract, support a revolution and the rest, they are producing something that someone else will react to in some way. They seek to connect with their audience and express an idea or emotion which has the capacity to enrich our experience of life itself.

question_groups.instructions:
Reading Passage 2 has seven paragraphs, A-G.
Which paragraph contains the following information?
Write the correct letter in boxes 1-5 on your answer sheet.

questions.text: a claim that artists may have no clear objective when creating a piece of art
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Câu hỏi này muốn tìm đoạn văn nào có chứa một nhận định rằng nghệ sĩ có thể không có một mục tiêu (objective) rõ ràng nào khi họ tạo ra một tác phẩm nghệ thuật.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong câu hỏi:
artists ~ artists
no aim or goal is necessarily required ~ no clear objective
may just make a work of art because they feel compelled to ~ may have no clear objective when creating a piece of art

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Đoạn B chỉ rõ: "Nhưng tương tự, nghệ sĩ có thể chỉ tạo ra một tác phẩm nghệ thuật bởi vì họ cảm thấy buộc phải làm vậy. Bởi vì tác phẩm tự nó là sự biện minh cho chính nó, không nhất thiết cần một mục tiêu hay mục đích nào để giải thích, hoặc ít hơn nữa, để biện minh cho sự tồn tại của nó."
=> Thông tin này cho thấy đoạn B đã "đưa ra một nhận định rằng nghệ sĩ có thể không có mục tiêu rõ ràng khi sáng tạo một tác phẩm nghệ thuật".

Bước 4: Đáp án: B
quotes: But equally, artists may just make a work of art because they feel compelled to. Because the work is its own justification, no aim or goal is necessarily required to explain or, still less, to justify its existence.

questions.text: a description of how artists hope to benefit other people
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Câu hỏi này yêu cầu tìm đoạn văn mô tả cách mà các nghệ sĩ hy vọng sẽ mang lại lợi ích (benefit) cho người khác.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong câu hỏi:
artists ~ artists
enrich our experience of life itself ~ benefit other people
seek to connect with their audience ~ hope to

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Đoạn G chỉ rõ: "Khi các nghệ sĩ làm việc để phản hồi và thể hiện ý tưởng... họ đang tạo ra thứ gì đó mà người khác sẽ phản ứng theo một cách nào đó. Họ tìm cách kết nối với khán giả của mình và thể hiện một ý tưởng hoặc cảm xúc có khả năng làm phong phú thêm trải nghiệm sống của chúng ta."
=> Thông tin này cho thấy đoạn G đã "mô tả cách nghệ sĩ hy vọng mang lại lợi ích cho người khác thông qua việc kết nối và làm phong phú trải nghiệm sống".

Bước 4: Đáp án: G
quotes: They seek to connect with their audience and express an idea or emotion which has the capacity to enrich our experience of life itself.

questions.text: a comparison between the arts and things made to perform a particular function
quotes: The distinction here lies between things that are instrumental and things that are ends in themselves. An instrument exists for something beyond itself – namely, for what it can be used to do. We know that pictures are used as instruments in advertising, and the objective is always to persuade us to buy something. Similarly, music can be written chiefly to accompany dancing, or as a soundtrack to a movie. A play can be written to point out to the theatre audience a social injustice or other problems that should be dealt with. But even though the arts can sometimes be instrumental, that fact is not essential to their nature. What the arts are ’good for’ arises from their being an end in themselves, or more accurately, representing many different things that are valuable for their own sakes – such as, for instance, the creation of beauty.

questions.text: a claim that it's possible to convince the world that anything you have made is a work of art
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Câu hỏi này tìm đoạn văn nào chứa một nhận định (claim) rằng có thể thuyết phục (convince) cả thế giới rằng bất cứ thứ gì bạn tạo ra cũng là một tác phẩm nghệ thuật.

Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong câu hỏi:
Andy Warhol ~ (name associated with challenging art definitions)
whatever else (...) anyone can get away with in calling their creation a contribution to 'the arts' ~ possible to convince the world that anything you have made is a work of art

Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Đoạn D chỉ rõ: "Cụm từ 'nghệ thuật' bao gồm hội họa, điêu khắc, âm nhạc, văn học, khiêu vũ và biểu diễn sân khấu, và bất cứ thứ gì khác (trích lời nghệ sĩ nổi tiếng người Mỹ Andy Warhol) mà bất kỳ ai cũng có thể thành công trong việc gọi sáng tạo của họ là một đóng góp cho 'nghệ thuật'."
=> Thông tin này cho thấy đoạn D đã "đưa ra một nhận định rằng có thể thuyết phục thế giới rằng bất cứ thứ gì bạn tạo ra đều là một tác phẩm nghệ thuật, trích dẫn ý của Andy Warhol".

Bước 4: Đáp án: D
quotes: D. The phrase ’the arts’ includes painting, sculpture, music, literature, dance and theatre performance, and whatever else (to quote the famous US artist Andy Warhol) anyone can get away with in calling their creation a contribution to ’the arts’.

questions.text: an example of something that has an unintentional benefit for us
quotes: E. For a loose comparison, think of laughing at a joke. We do not laugh so that we can achieve a further goal – in order to be healthy or relaxed, say, even if we thereby succeed in being healthier or more relaxed – but simply because the joke has elicited that reaction. But although it is merely a reaction, laughing is, in fact, good for something nevertheless; it does make people feel better.

question_groups.instructions: Complete the summary below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 6-9 on your answer sheet.
question_groups.body:
The arts and human experience
Some people may claim that the arts serve no useful purpose, that they achieve nothing measurable and help nobody. But there are many clear examples of their usefulness, such as the inter-dependent relationship between music and ____ (6), or between the visual arts and the ____ (7) business. A dramatist may use a ____ (8) to draw our attention to various issues in society, for example some kind of injustice which needs correcting. Apart from these obvious practical benefits, there are other benefits that we gain from things, such as the ____ (9) we find in an artist's work.
question_groups.body_html:
The arts and human experience

Some people may claim that the arts serve no useful purpose, that they achieve nothing measurable and help nobody. But there are many clear examples of their usefulness, such as the inter-dependent relationship between music and [6], or between the visual arts and the [7] business. A dramatist may use a [8] to draw our attention to various issues in society, for example some kind of injustice which needs correcting. Apart from these obvious practical benefits, there are other benefits that we gain from things, such as the [9] we find in an artist's work.

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi và Giải thích ngữ pháp:
Có nhiều ví dụ rõ ràng về tính hữu ích của chúng, chẳng hạn như mối quan hệ phụ thuộc lẫn nhau giữa âm nhạc và _____.

Bước 2: Xác định loại từ dựa trên các dấu hiệu:
Loại từ: NOUN
Dấu hiệu: between music and + NOUN (NOUN làm Object của Preposition 'and')

Bước 3: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
inter-dependent relationship between music and ~ music can be written chiefly to accompany
practical benefits ~ instrumental uses

Bước 4: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Tương tự, âm nhạc có thể được viết chủ yếu để đi kèm với khiêu vũ, hoặc như một nhạc nền cho một bộ phim" (Similarly, music can be written chiefly to accompany dancing, or as a soundtrack to a movie).

Bước 5: Đáp án: dancing
Có nhiều ví dụ rõ ràng về tính hữu ích của chúng, chẳng hạn như mối quan hệ phụ thuộc lẫn nhau giữa âm nhạc và khiêu vũ (There are many clear examples of their usefulness, such as the inter-dependent relationship between music and dancing).
quotes: Similarly, music can be written chiefly to accompany dancing, or as a soundtrack to a movie.

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi và Giải thích ngữ pháp:
hoặc giữa nghệ thuật thị giác và ngành kinh doanh _____.

Bước 2: Xác định loại từ dựa trên các dấu hiệu:
Loại từ: NOUN
Dấu hiệu: the + NOUN + business (NOUN làm Adjective bổ nghĩa cho Noun 'business')

Bước 3: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
visual arts ~ pictures
business ~ commercial use/industry

Bước 4: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Chúng ta biết rằng hình ảnh được sử dụng như những công cụ trong quảng cáo, và mục tiêu luôn là thuyết phục chúng ta mua thứ gì đó" (We know that pictures are used as instruments in advertising, and the objective is always to persuade us to buy something).

Bước 5: Đáp án: advertising
hoặc giữa nghệ thuật thị giác và ngành kinh doanh quảng cáo (or between the visual arts and the advertising business).
quotes: We know that pictures are used as instruments in advertising, and the objective is always to persuade us to buy something.

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi và Giải thích ngữ pháp:
Một nhà viết kịch có thể sử dụng một _____ để thu hút sự chú ý của chúng ta đến các vấn đề khác nhau trong xã hội.

Bước 2: Xác định loại từ dựa trên các dấu hiệu:
Loại từ: NOUN
Dấu hiệu: use a + NOUN (NOUN làm Object của Transitive verb 'use')

Bước 3: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
dramatist ~ playwright/theatre
draw our attention to various issues in society ~ point out social injustice or other problems

Bước 4: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Một vở kịch có thể được viết để chỉ ra cho khán giả trong rạp hát một sự bất công xã hội hoặc các vấn đề khác cần được giải quyết" (A play can be written to point out to the theatre audience a social injustice or other problems that should be dealt with).

Bước 5: Đáp án: play
Một nhà viết kịch có thể sử dụng một vở kịch để thu hút sự chú ý của chúng ta đến các vấn đề khác nhau trong xã hội (A dramatist may use a play to draw our attention to various issues in society).
quotes: A play can be written to point out to the theatre audience a social injustice or other problems that should be dealt with.

What the arts are ’good for’ arises from their being an end in themselves, or more accurately, representing many different things that are valuable for their own sakes – such as, for instance, the creation of beauty.
